commits.edited_message:
lib: Drop XML_ATTR_INFO code (XML_GetAttributeInfo, struct XML_AttrInfo)

While removing the per-attribute XML_AttrInfo bookkeeping, also stop
over-allocating the per-binding buffer that stores expanded
(namespace-qualified) element names.  That buffer only has to hold
localPart + URI + prefix, so reserve exactly that length instead of
padding every (re)allocation with a fixed EXPAND_SPARE slop.

(cherry picked from commit 46d314afff54a668b742ab479313dc736f51a432)

lib|tests: Replace assert with runtime overflow check in expat_realloc

In expat_realloc, the size passed to realloc_fcn is calculated as
sizeof(size_t) + EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING + size. Previously, expat_realloc
relied on an assertion:
assert(SIZE_MAX - sizeof(size_t) - EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING >= size);
under the assumption that preceding accounting checks and parser
invariants preclude reaching an overflow state in practice.

However, in release builds compiled with NDEBUG, assertions are
compiled out. Replace the assert with an explicit runtime check:
if (size > SIZE_MAX - sizeof(size_t) - EXPAT_MALLOC_PADDING) {
  return NULL;
}
immediately preceding the addition, ensuring consistent defensive
behavior across all build configurations.

While hardening, also make storeAtts() always NUL-terminate the
expanded namespace-qualified name at its full length, so the buffer
is terminated regardless of which expansion branch produced it.

Also extend test_alloc_tracker_size_recorded in alloc_tests.c to
exercise SIZE_MAX and SIZE_MAX / 2 with expat_realloc, verifying
that the allocation fails and the recorded size remains unchanged.

Signed-off-by: Filippo Tedeschi <filippotedeschi98@gmail.com>
(cherry picked from commit 69edbec09f2cd3e0bd6e0a093b55ea38af902d7d)

coupling:
The reachable heap-buffer-overflow (storeAtts(), expanded namespace-qualified element name) emerges ONLY from the composition of the two edited commits; each diff is correct maintenance on its own.

- Commit e68ecd9 (Edit A): the per-binding expanded-name buffer is reserved with exactly `totalLen` bytes instead of `totalLen + EXPAND_SPARE`. This is correct in isolation: storeAtts() and the end-tag rewrite in doContent() only ever write indices 0..totalLen-1 (localPart + URI + prefix + one NUL), so an exact-size reservation is sufficient. Reviewed alone, nothing writes past totalLen-1, so dropping the slack is benign.

- Commit 771d7cb (Edit B): storeAtts() unconditionally writes a NUL terminator at index `totalLen` (one past the last content element). This is correct in isolation too: in the unedited tree every expanded-name buffer carries EXPAND_SPARE (24) extra elements, so index totalLen is comfortably inside the allocation. Reviewed alone, the write is in-bounds.

Only with BOTH edits present does the buffer become exactly `totalLen` elements AND get written at index `totalLen` -> 1-element heap-buffer-overflow WRITE.

The fix is necessarily non-local: fixing only e68ecd9 (restore EXPAND_SPARE) OR only 771d7cb (drop/last-index the extra NUL) each removes the overflow, but neither single diff looks wrong on its own, so a commit-by-commit reviewer must correlate the reservation in e68ecd9 with the write in 771d7cb to see and repair the defect. Verified: base (main) clean; base + only Edit A clean; base + only Edit B clean; both edits -> ASan heap-buffer-overflow at storeAtts (lib/xmlparse.c).
